lead.headline: Iran rejects Trump's Hormuz claim as two more tankers are hit
lead.dek: The UAE called the attacks piracy; 15 of the company's ships have been hit since February.
body: Two vessels tied to Abu Dhabi's national oil company were attacked while crossing the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday evening, hours after Iran's military dismissed President Donald Trump's claim of American control of the waterway as lies.

ADNOC said nobody was hurt. It was the second attack on the company's ships in days and the 15th since February. The UAE foreign ministry called Iran's use of the strait as economic coercion piracy and a direct threat to the region. Iran did not comment.

Trump said Wednesday the United States has total control of the strait; Iran's central military command said it is under the complete control of the Islamic Republic. Eight ships crossed Tuesday, the fewest since Aug. 5.

briefs.headline: Judge dismisses U.S. antisemitism suit against Harvard
briefs.summary: Judge Richard Stearns called the cited incidents too isolated and episodic to show a persistent violation. The government said it is weighing next steps.

briefs.headline: Three states execute prisoners on the same day
briefs.summary: Oklahoma, Tennessee and Alabama carried out lethal injections Thursday, the first same-day trio since Jan. 7, 2010, and the 21st execution this year.

briefs.headline: Wildfires force evacuations in Germany, France and Croatia
briefs.summary: About 1,800 left the German village of Gey and 525 the Landes in France; 14 were hospitalized in Split. Some 500,000 hectares have burned in the EU.

briefs.headline: Farage retakes the Clacton seat he resigned in July
briefs.summary: He took 22,239 votes to 9,455 for the satirist Count Binface on 44% turnout, with the main parties boycotting.

briefs.headline: Taiwan slows mobile internet in an invasion drill
briefs.summary: Carriers cut speeds to 256 Kbps for 30 minutes Thursday in Taipei and six other places during the Han Kuang exercises.

briefs.headline: Safety board says Institute plant required no respirators
briefs.summary: The Chemical Safety Board said workers at Ames Goldsmith Catalyst Refiners had no gas monitors when mixed chemicals released hydrogen sulfide April 22, killing two.

briefs.headline: Justice family says it will close the Greenbrier casino
briefs.summary: A federal court filing said about 90 workers would be laid off so a $500M refinancing can close, with delays costing about $145,000 a day.

regional.item: An independent tester told a town hall the July warehouse fire's plume reached 10,000 feet across 35 miles.

briefs.headline: Nigeria miss the Women's World Cup for the first time
briefs.summary: South Africa won 2-1 through Thembi Kgatlana and Refiloe Jane to take one of Africa's two playoff places. Ghana beat Ivory Coast 2-1.

briefs.headline: Swiatek beats Rybakina for her first title of the season
briefs.summary: The Pole won 6-2, 6-3 in the Canadian Open final in Toronto and moves back into the top five from No. 8.

briefs.headline: Marshall women open with a 3-1 win over Morehead State
briefs.summary: Luana Gusmao scored twice in seven minutes at Huntington on Thursday; Delfina Lombardo added the third.

briefs.headline: Hibernating mice keep memories after losing synapses
briefs.summary: More than half of hippocampal synapses vanished during artificial hibernation, yet recall held or improved, the Okinawa team reported in Science.

briefs.headline: Gut viruses carry mutation hotspots that beat bacteria
briefs.summary: Repetitive stretches in a phage gene mutate thousands of times faster than the rest of the genome, letting the virus route around bacterial defenses.
